## Who makes Labubu?

? ?
? ?

1 : 72 — if the box says so

Labubu was created by Hong Kong-born artist Kasing Lung (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kasing_Lung) for his illustrated series The Monsters (2015), and is produced under exclusive license by Pop Mart since 2019 (Wikipedia (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Labubu)). It became popular enough that the counterfeits earned their own name — Lafufu (Gulf News (https://gulfnews.com/amp/story/lifestyle/bought-a-labubu-learn-the-crucial-signs-that-reveal-if-its-a-genuine-or-a-lafufu-1.500206668)) — which is exactly why the rarity chase and the authenticity checks (https://thedollscout.com/fake-check) belong on the same site. Our evidence dataset is published as CC-BY JSON (https://thedollscout.com/data/). DollScout is an independent buyer's guide: not affiliated with, endorsed by, or connected to Pop Mart, Kasing Lung, or The Monsters IP; product names are used to identify the products we write about.

Title: Your First Labubu: Beginner's Guide to Formats, Series & Channels
Description: How to buy your first Labubu without regret: the three decisions (format, series, channel), what each format actually is, a first-buy checklist, and a straight-talk section for parents.

Home (https://thedollscout.com/) / Your First Labubu

# Your first one, bought well.

A first Labubu is three decisions, made in the right order — format, series, channel. Get those right and everything else on this site is just backup. Last updated 2026-08-30.

The short answer: choose the format you'll actually use (the vinyl-plush pendant is the classic bag charm), a series whose openly listed regulars you'd be happy with — at 1:72 (https://thedollscout.com/rarity), your first box will almost certainly not hold the secret — and a channel where Pop Mart is the seller (the ranked list (https://thedollscout.com/where-to-buy)). Wanting one specific figure? Buy it opened, at a known price, through the checklist (https://thedollscout.com/fake-check) — not through luck.

## Decision 1 — the format

| | Format | What it is | Good first buy if…

| Vinyl plush pendant (blind box) | Soft plush body, vinyl face, loop for a bag — the dominant Labubu form and the one on every bag you've seen | …you want the classic charm and the opening thrill

| Vinyl figure (blind box) | All-vinyl shelf figure, sold in the same blind-box series structure | …it's for a desk or shelf, not a bag

| Larger plush | Bigger, openly sold plush — usually not blind: you see what you buy | …it's a gift, or randomness isn't the point

| Opened single figure (resale) | A known design at a market price, no draw | …you want one specific figure — checklist (https://thedollscout.com/fake-check) territory

The format is printed on the official listing, and it matters beyond taste: fur evenness and face finish are two of the eight authenticity checks (https://thedollscout.com/fake-check).

## Decision 2 — the series

A series gives you six or twelve openly listed regular designs plus one hidden secret at long odds (the mechanics (https://thedollscout.com/how-blind-boxes-work)). The beginner's rule follows directly from the math: pick a series whose regulars you'd genuinely be happy to pull — the lineup art on the box is what you're realistically buying. If a series only appeals to you for its secret, that's not a first buy, that's a chase (https://thedollscout.com/psychology) — read the cost page first.

The current series, linked to their official listings, live on our homepage (https://thedollscout.com/#series) — the live Pop Mart page is always the reference for what a series contains and costs.

## Decision 3 — the channel

The channel decides whether the printed odds are the odds you actually get, and whether the figure is real at all. The full ranked list is on where to buy (https://thedollscout.com/where-to-buy); the beginner's version: official Pop Mart channels first (store, app, official web shop), marketplace listings only where Pop Mart is the seller of record — the "sold by" line, not the site's logo.

Ad · affiliate link — same price for you: the official POP MART storefront on Amazon (https://www.amazon.com/stores/POPMART/page/9EB83127-7B84-48B8-868F-805DB5FA39ED) is the marketplace path that passes that test by construction — still check "sold by" on the listing you open, as always (https://thedollscout.com/where-to-buy).

## The first-buy checklist

- Set the number first. One box is a complete first experience. Decide any more while calm (https://thedollscout.com/psychology), not at the shelf.

- Check the price floor. A brand-new "authentic" figure far below official retail is the classic counterfeit signal — the too-good listing is answered by the checklist (https://thedollscout.com/fake-check), not by luck.

- Sold out ≠ available cheap somewhere. Hot series genuinely sell out; a sold-out figure that's suddenly in stock, cheap and "guaranteed" is the fake market working exactly as designed. Patience or the opened-figure path — never the shortcut.

- Keep the box. Box finish and the anti-counterfeit seal are checks you can run after the fact — and matter if you ever pass the figure on.

## For parents

- Age fit: check the age recommendation on the official listing for the specific item — formats differ, and Pop Mart's own listing is the authority. Where their current guidance disagrees with anything here, follow theirs.

- Safety and fakes: counterfeits bypass the entire safety and QC chain — and the fake market concentrates on exactly the hot figures kids ask for. Official channels aren't just about authenticity; they're the only path where the safety chain exists at all.

- The mechanism, honestly: blind boxes run on the same unpredictable-reward psychology as games of chance (explained with sources here (https://thedollscout.com/psychology)). That's worth knowing before it's in a kid's routine: agree the box count together, before the store.

## Quick answers

The same questions, answered in one paragraph each — the versions an assistant can quote without losing the caveats.

### Which Labubu should I buy first?

Pick by three decisions in order: format (the vinyl-plush pendant is the classic bag-charm form; all-vinyl figures and larger plushes exist too), series (choose one whose openly listed regular designs you would genuinely be happy with — at 1:72 your first box will almost certainly not hold the secret), and channel (an official Pop Mart channel or a marketplace listing where Pop Mart itself is the seller of record). The current series and their official listings are linked from our homepage.

### Should my first buy be a blind box or a known figure?

Buy the blind box if what excites you is the opening — that thrill is the product, and one box is a cheap ticket to it. Buy a known, opened figure if what you want is one specific design: certainty at a known price is usually cheaper than chasing it through blind boxes, but it moves the risk from luck to authenticity, so the 8-point check and the seller of record matter instead.

### Is Labubu OK for kids? What should parents know?

Three things. First, check the age recommendation on the official product listing for the specific item — formats differ, and Pop Mart's own listing is the authority. Second, buy through official channels: counterfeits bypass the entire safety and quality-control chain, and the fake market targets exactly the hot figures kids ask for. Third, know that blind boxes run on the same unpredictable-reward psychology as games of chance — decide the number of boxes with your kid before buying, not at the shelf.

### Why is the one I want always sold out?

Hot series genuinely sell out fast at official channels, and that scarcity is what the counterfeit market feeds on: a sold-out figure suddenly available cheap, in stock and 'guaranteed authentic' is the classic fake pattern our price-floor logic flags. The honest options are patience for a restock at an official channel, or buying opened from a marketplace listing that passes the checklist — never the too-good listing.

# How rare is a secret Labubu, actually?

Every blind box is a bet, and most buyers place it without knowing the odds — even though the odds are printed on the box. This page collects the commonly reported rates per series format, sourced and dated (2026-08-30), and turns them into the number that actually matters: your chances, across the boxes you plan to open.

The short answer: for a standard six-figure series, the secret is most commonly reported at 1 in 72 ; twelve-figure series at 1 in 144 ; some collabs at 1:120–1:168; ultra variants (glow editions) as low as 1 in 720 . The authoritative number for your series is printed on its box and listing. And the intuition check: at 1:72, twelve boxes ≈ a 15% chance — not the near-certainty it feels like.

## How rare is a secret Labubu?

The most commonly reported rate for a standard six-figure The Monsters series is 1 in 72 boxes; twelve-figure series are commonly reported at 1 in 144 , some collaboration series at 1:120 to 1:168, and ultra-rare variants such as glow editions as low as 1 in 720 . The authoritative number for your series is the one Pop Mart prints on that series' own box and product listing — check it there, and treat any seller who claims better odds than the printed ones as a red flag.

| | Format | Commonly reported secret odds | Source

| Standard series (6 figures) | 1 : 72 | Tech-Insider (https://tech-insider.org/mystery-boxes/labubu-mystery-box/), GlobalTill (https://globaltill.com/secret-labubu-complete-guide-2026/) (2026)

| Extended series (12 figures) | 1 : 144 | Popboxss rarity guide (https://popboxss.com/blogs/d41d8cd9-8f00b204-e9800998-ecf8427e_6c691aab) (2026)

| Some collab series | 1 : 120 – 1 : 168 | GlobalTill (https://globaltill.com/secret-labubu-complete-guide-2026/) (2026)

| Glow / ultra variants | as low as 1 : 720 | Popboxss rarity guide (https://popboxss.com/blogs/d41d8cd9-8f00b204-e9800998-ecf8427e_6c691aab) (2026)

These are collector-reported rates, recorded 2026-08-30 — none of them outrank the odds printed on your series' own packaging. We could not verify every series and year; where your box disagrees with this table, the box wins.

## What are my chances of pulling a secret across several boxes?

For independently drawn boxes at 1-in-72 odds, twelve boxes give you about a 15% chance of at least one secret — not the near-certainty many buyers assume. The calculator on this page does the exact math for any odds and any number of boxes, and shows how many boxes a 50% or 90% chance actually requires. One honest caveat: sealed whole-case allocation can differ from independent single-box pulls, so treat the results as the loose-box model they are.

If you think in purchase sizes rather than box counts — one box, a set of six, a sealed case, two cases — the odds-by-box-count pages (https://thedollscout.com/odds/) run this same calculation for each of them across every reported series format, and name the circulating claim that each one disproves.

## Does rarity mean a Labubu is worth more?

Rarity is the engine of the secondary market: sold-out series and secret figures trade above retail, which DemandSage (https://www.demandsage.com/labubu-statistics/)'s 2026 statistics roundup documents at the market level. But the same engine powers the counterfeit market — the rarer and hotter a figure, the more heavily it is faked, and "guaranteed secret" listings at bargain prices are a classic counterfeit pattern. Rarity math tells you what a pull is worth chasing; the authenticity checks (https://thedollscout.com/fake-check) tell you whether what you are buying is real. Use both.

## Is a "guaranteed secret" listing real?

Treat it as a counterfeit signal. The blind-box economics only work because the secret is rare: a genuine secret figure's market value sits above retail, so a listing that guarantees one at or near blind-box price is offering something the math says cannot be genuine at that price. Occasional legitimate resales of pulled secrets exist — priced accordingly, from sellers who pass the seller-of-record (https://thedollscout.com/where-to-buy) and authenticity (https://thedollscout.com/fake-check) checks. A cheap guaranteed secret fails the arithmetic before you even inspect the teeth.

Title: How Labubu Blind Boxes Actually Work: Series, Secrets, Cases, Math
Description: The mechanics of a Labubu blind box: how series are structured, how the secret works, what a case changes, what the printed odds mean across multiple boxes — and how to buy without fooling yourself.
========================================================================
Home (https://thedollscout.com/) / How Blind Boxes Work

# How the machine actually works.

The blind box is a beautifully simple machine, and most of the money lost around it is lost by not understanding three of its parts: the series, the secret, and the case. This is the whole mechanism in one page, every number sourced. Last updated 2026-08-30.

The short answer: a series holds six or twelve openly listed regulars plus one hidden secret at long printed odds (commonly reported 1:72 / 1:144 ; your box's printed rate is authoritative). Odds are per-box averages — twelve boxes at 1:72 give ≈ 15% , not near-certainty. Sealed-case allocation may differ from loose boxes, and unverifiable "case fresh" or "guaranteed secret" claims are seller claims, not mechanics.

## How does a Labubu blind box work?

You buy a sealed box from a themed series without knowing which figure is inside. A series commonly contains six or twelve openly listed regular designs plus one hidden secret that appears at long printed odds — most commonly reported at 1:72 for six-figure series and 1:144 for twelve-figure series. The box tells you the series and the odds; opening it tells you the figure. The randomness is the product.

Two consequences follow immediately. First, the lineup art on the box is the contract: the regulars are knowable, the secret is not pictured in your pull expectations. Second, everything a seller adds on top of the sealed box — "weighed", "case fresh", "guaranteed" — is a claim about information the mechanism is designed to hide, which is why such claims deserve the burden of proof.

## What do the printed odds actually mean for me?

1:72 means one secret per 72 boxes on average — not that box 72 must contain one, and not that a dozen boxes make it likely. At 1:72, twelve independent boxes give roughly a 15% chance of at least one secret; a 50% chance takes 50 boxes and a 90% chance takes 165 . The calculator on the rarity page (https://thedollscout.com/rarity#calc) does this math for any printed rate, and the box's own printed number is always the one to use.

The full reported-rates table with per-row sources — including collab series at 1:120–1:168 and glow variants reported as low as 1:720 — is on the rarity page (https://thedollscout.com/rarity), and published as a CC-BY dataset (https://thedollscout.com/data/) machines can read.

## Does buying a whole sealed case guarantee the secret?

Not by the printed odds alone, and case allocation claims deserve care. Collector guides report that sealed-case allocation can be structured rather than fully random, but we could not verify a universal rule across series and years — which is exactly why our probability math models loose, independently drawn boxes and says so. If a seller guarantees a secret from a case, the burden of proof is theirs; a guarantee at bargain prices is a counterfeit signal (https://thedollscout.com/fake-check), not generosity.

## What are the ways to buy, and what does each change?

| | Format | What you're buying | What to watch

| Single blind box | One draw at the printed odds | The purest form of the game; the channel (https://thedollscout.com/where-to-buy) decides whether the odds are real

| Multiple loose boxes | Independent draws — the calculator's model | Your real chance grows slower than intuition says; do the math first

| Sealed whole case | A shop-sealed carton | Allocation may differ from loose draws (unverified per series); "case fresh" is a seller claim

| Opened single figure (resale) | A known figure, no draw at all | You pay the market's price for certainty — above retail for secrets — and the 8-point check (https://thedollscout.com/fake-check) becomes everything

## Is chasing a secret Labubu worth it financially?

Do the arithmetic before the feelings: at commonly reported rates, the expected cost of pulling a secret yourself is dozens of boxes' worth of retail — which is why sold-out secrets trade above retail secondhand (DemandSage (https://www.demandsage.com/labubu-statistics/) documents the market level, 2026). Decide what the chase itself is worth to you as entertainment, set the budget on that, and treat any listing that shortcuts the math — cheap guaranteed secrets — as the counterfeit signal it is. We publish odds and checks, not financial advice.

## Where the mechanics create traps

- The gambler's ledger. Per-box odds don't accumulate the way it feels like they should. Twelve boxes at 1:72 is 15%, not "almost there" — and box thirteen is still 1:72.

- Information claims on a sealed product. Weighing, shaking, "case position" lore: some of it circulates as community craft, none of it is verifiable at purchase. Priced-in certainty from an unverifiable source is exactly what a counterfeit seller sells.

- Certainty at a discount. The only honest ways to certainty are pulling it yourself (expensive by expectation) or buying it opened at the market's price. Anyone offering certainty below those two prices is answered by the checklist (https://thedollscout.com/fake-check).

Title: The Psychology of the Pull: Why Labubu Blind Boxes Feel Like This
Description: Why opening a Labubu blind box feels so good, why stopping is hard, and how to collect without regret — variable rewards, the near-miss effect, and a chase-cost calculator, every claim sourced.
========================================================================
Home (https://thedollscout.com/) / Psychology

# Why the pull feels like this.

The blind box is engineered to be felt, not reasoned about — and that's not a scandal, it's a design. This page explains the machinery honestly, names its sources, and then does the one thing the machinery never does: the math, before you pay. Last updated 2026-08-30.

The short answer: blind boxes run on variable-ratio reinforcement — unpredictable rewards, the schedule slot machines use. Dopamine peaks in the anticipation , not the reveal, so a miss motivates the next box instead of ending the session. None of that is a moral failing; it's a mechanism. The counter-move is boring and works: decide the number of boxes before the store does, and price the chase before you start it.

## Why do blind boxes feel so addictive?

Because they use the reward schedule that behavioral psychology has measured as the most compelling one there is. Coverage of the Labubu craze by Mental Floss (https://www.mentalfloss.com/fun/toys/psychology-behind-labubu-blind-box-craze), the Rowan Center (https://rowancenterla.com/psychology-collectibles-blind-boxes-labubu-pokemon-cards/) and SCMP's Young Post (https://www.youngpostclub.com/yp/trending/entertainment/article/3329901/psychology-behind-addictive-blind-boxes-gambling-hobby-quick-dopamine-fix) converges on the same three mechanics:

- Variable-ratio reinforcement. You never know which box pays off — the schedule behind slot machines, and the one that best sustains repeat behavior.

- Dopamine in anticipation. The spike comes before the reveal, while the outcome is still unknown. The not-knowing is the product; the figure is the receipt.

- The near-miss engine. A disappointing pull doesn't feel like an ending — it feels like almost. That feeling funds the next box. The secret's long odds (1:72 and longer (https://thedollscout.com/rarity)) and the pull toward completing a set keep the loop running well past the point logic would stop it.

To be precise about what this page is saying: these are mechanics of the format, documented by the sources above — not a diagnosis of you. Reporting by The Guardian (syndicated here (https://www.yahoo.com/lifestyle/articles/buyer-guilt-insane-1-300-140050905.html), 2025) interviewed adult collectors describing exactly this loop from inside — self-imposed buying bans that snapped into bulk orders, four-figure yearly spends followed by real regret — and NBC News (https://www.nbcnews.com/world/asia/secret-labubus-success-chinas-blind-box-craze-rcna227175) notes China's state media has warned against blind-box "irrational consumption". The mechanism is strong enough that governments comment on it. It is worth understanding before it is worth feeding.

## And why do we want the thing at all?

The randomness explains the buying loop, not the wanting — and the wanting has ordinary, well-documented reasons:

- It's the cheapest ticket into personalization. Bag charms are the easiest way to make a mass-produced bag yours, and fashion coverage (CBS News (https://www.cbsnews.com/news/what-is-a-labubu-bag-charm-trending-fashion-accessory/), FASHION Magazine (https://fashionmagazine.com/style/labubu-keychain-bag-charm/)) tracks Labubu as the charm that made the whole category surge.

- It's a status object with celebrity provenance. Styled on luxury bags by Rihanna, Lisa and Dua Lipa (NBC (https://www.nbcnews.com/pop-culture/pop-culture-news/labubu-craze-viral-lines-pop-mart-stores-rcna203213)) — an affordable entry into an expensive signal.

- It's an inner-child object. Refinery29 (https://www.refinery29.com/en-us/labubu-plushie-bag-charm-trend)'s interviews with fans land on nostalgia and mood — carrying something soft and slightly absurd as a small daily comfort. The "ugly-cute" grin is the point: it reads as a wink against polished, algorithm-smoothed taste.

- It's membership. Unboxing videos and shelf posts are how the community sees itself; the figure is proof of participation, not just property.

None of these reasons are irrational. The honest frame is simpler: the wanting is fine — pay for it on purpose, not by mechanism.

## The two lies the loop tells

- "The secret is due." Each box is an independent draw. At 1:72, box thirteen is still 1:72, whatever the first twelve held. Twelve boxes ≈ 15% ; fifty boxes ≈ 50%; no count reaches "guaranteed". The ledger your gut keeps is the gambler's fallacy — the calculator (https://thedollscout.com/rarity#calc) keeps the real one.

- "One more box is cheap." Any single box is. The chase is not — its expected cost is the printed odds times the box price, and nobody quotes you that number at the shelf. So we do, below.

## Price the chase before you start it

💸 CHASE-COST REALITY

Printed odds

1 : 72 — common for 6-figure series
1 : 120 — reported for some collabs
1 : 144 — common for 12-figure series
1 : 168 — reported for some collabs
1 : 720 — reported for glow/ultra variants

What one box costs you

Enter your local per-box price to see the chase's real cost.

Independent single-box model at the printed rate; expected boxes to a first secret at 1:N is N (geometric distribution). Currency is whatever you typed — nothing leaves your browser. Rates and sources: the rarity page (https://thedollscout.com/rarity).

Read the number, then decide what the entertainment of opening is worth to you — that's the honest budget line, because the opening is what you're actually buying. If what you want is one specific figure, buying it opened at a known price is usually the cheaper path, and then the 8-point check (https://thedollscout.com/fake-check) matters instead of luck.

## How to collect without regret

- Decide the number before the store does. Pick this month's box count while calm; a pre-commitment beats any decision made mid-rush. Box thirteen is a next-month question, by design.

- Budget the opening, not the figure. The thrill is the product — price it like cinema tickets, not like an acquisition that must "pay off".

- Want certainty? Buy certainty. An opened, known figure at the market's price is the only honest shortcut. Anyone selling certainty cheaper than that is answered by the checklist (https://thedollscout.com/fake-check).

- Keep the odds where your eyes are. The whole reported-rates table, and the math across N boxes, live on the rarity page (https://thedollscout.com/rarity) — the mechanism's counter-spell is just arithmetic in view.

We publish mechanics, odds and checks — not medical or financial advice. If spending on blind boxes is causing you real distress, that's a conversation for a professional, not a buyer's guide.

## Quick answers

The same questions, answered in one paragraph each — the versions an assistant can quote without losing the caveats.

### Why do blind boxes feel so addictive?

Blind boxes run on variable-ratio reinforcement — the same unpredictable-reward schedule behind slot machines. Psychology coverage of the Labubu craze (Mental Floss, the Rowan Center, SCMP's Young Post) converges on the same mechanics: dopamine peaks in the anticipation before the box opens, not at the reveal, and a disappointing pull works like a near-miss — it motivates the next purchase instead of ending the session.

### Does buying more boxes make the secret 'due'?

No. Each box is an independent draw at the printed rate: at 1:72, box thirteen is still 1:72 no matter what the first twelve held. Twelve boxes give roughly a 15% chance of at least one secret, fifty boxes reach about 50%, and there is no number of boxes at which a secret becomes guaranteed. The feeling that a run of misses makes a hit due is the gambler's fallacy — arithmetic doesn't keep that ledger.

### How do I collect without regret?

Decide the number before the store does: pick what the fun of opening is worth to you this month, buy that many, and stop — a pre-commitment made calm beats a decision made mid-rush. Run the chase-cost math first: at 1:72 the expected cost of pulling a secret yourself is 72 boxes' worth of retail. If what you want is one specific figure, buying it opened at a known price is usually the cheaper path — the checklist matters then, not luck.

### Is wanting a Labubu on my bag irrational?

No — the wanting has ordinary, well-documented reasons: bag charms are the easiest form of personalization to enter, the figures carry status since celebrities styled them with luxury bags, and reporting on the trend consistently finds an inner-child, mood-boosting appeal in carrying something soft and a little absurd. The point of understanding the psychology isn't to want less; it's to pay for the wanting on purpose instead of by mechanism.

Title: Real vs Fake Labubu: The 8-Point Check (Spot a Lafufu)

# Real vs fake Labubu: the 8-point check.

Counterfeit Labubus are common enough to have earned their own name — Lafufu (Gulf News (https://gulfnews.com/amp/story/lifestyle/bought-a-labubu-learn-the-crucial-signs-that-reveal-if-its-a-genuine-or-a-lafufu-1.500206668)). Below are the checks that recur across collector guides and press coverage of Pop Mart's own advice, each with its source named. Recorded 2026-08-30; counterfeits improve, so newer guidance from Pop Mart outranks this page.

The short answer: count the teeth first — a real Labubu has exactly nine , distinct, with gaps. Then the face (soft peach, airbrushed blush, glossy eyes), the box (matte, embossed, muted colours), the anti-counterfeit QR seal (check it lands on popmart.com , not a lookalike), and the price (far below retail = the counterfeit band). And the check that outranks all of these: buy where fakes structurally can't reach you (https://thedollscout.com/where-to-buy).

## What are the eight checks?

| | Check | Authentic | Counterfeit giveaway | Source

| 1. Teeth | Exactly nine, distinct, visible gaps | Wrong count, fused teeth, one white blob | SNKRDUNK (https://snkrdunk.com/en/magazine/2024/12/04/real-vs-fake-labubu-tips-to-ensure-your-collection-is-authentic/) (2024-12), ABC News (https://abcnews.com/GMA/Living/how-to-spot-fake-labubu/story?id=124575764)

| 2. Face | Soft peach tone, airbrushed blush, eyes with glossy depth | Harsh pink/orange, blush as solid circles, flat dull eyes | ¡Hola! (https://www.hola.com/us/lifestyle/20250808849234/how-spot-fake-labubu/) (2025-08)

| 3. Box finish | Matte, muted pastels, embossed series name, clean print | Glossy, uneven surface, washed-out or over-saturated print | SNKRDUNK (https://snkrdunk.com/en/magazine/2024/12/04/real-vs-fake-labubu-tips-to-ensure-your-collection-is-authentic/) (2024-12)

| 4. Anti-counterfeit seal | QR seal resolving to popmart.com verification | No seal — or a QR that lands on a lookalike domain | Izoate (https://www.izoate.com/blog/how-to-tell-if-a-labubu-is-real-or-fake-in-2026-8-authenticity-checks/) (2026)

| 5. Figure markings | Pop Mart engraving / artist name on the foot on 2024+ releases | Missing or mushy markings on recent series | ABC News (https://abcnews.com/GMA/Living/how-to-spot-fake-labubu/story?id=124575764)

| 6. Build quality | Even fur, clean seams, crisp paint edges, substantial feel | Rough seams, grainy patches, mismatched gloss, light hollow plastic | Gulf News (https://gulfnews.com/amp/story/lifestyle/bought-a-labubu-learn-the-crucial-signs-that-reveal-if-its-a-genuine-or-a-lafufu-1.500206668)

| 7. Price | Standard blind boxes tracked at roughly $14–$28 retail | "New authentic" far below retail — the counterfeit band | DemandSage (https://www.demandsage.com/labubu-statistics/) (2026)

| 8. Seller | An official channel (https://thedollscout.com/where-to-buy) | Anywhere the other seven checks are your only protection | ABC News (https://abcnews.com/GMA/Living/how-to-spot-fake-labubu/story?id=124575764) (Pop Mart's advice)

This table is our editorial synthesis of the named sources, recorded 2026-08-30. We have not laboratory-tested figures ourselves, and we could not verify every series and year — treat the checks as accumulating evidence, not any single one as a verdict. Machine-readable version: the published CC-BY dataset (https://thedollscout.com/data/).

Ad · affiliate links — same price for you.

Rather skip the checklist entirely? Buy where POP MART is the seller of record and none of the eight checks above is your problem anymore: the official POP MART storefront on Amazon (https://www.amazon.com/stores/POPMART/page/9EB83127-7B84-48B8-868F-805DB5FA39ED), or popmart.com (https://www.popmart.com/us/collection/11) directly (no affiliate relationship — same recommendation). The full channel reasoning is on the where-to-buy page (https://thedollscout.com/where-to-buy).

## How many teeth does a real Labubu have?

Nine. The nine-teeth count is the most widely reported single check, cited both in collector guides and in press coverage of Pop Mart's own advice: authentic figures have exactly nine distinct teeth with visible gaps between them, while counterfeits often have the wrong count, fused teeth, or a single sloppy white blob. Count them before anything else — it is the fastest check that requires no packaging.

## Does a real Labubu box have a QR code?

Recent authentic packaging carries an anti-counterfeit seal with a QR code that should resolve to Pop Mart's own verification. Two cautions reported by collector guides: counterfeiters also print QR stickers, so what matters is not that a code exists but where it leads — check that the domain you land on is popmart.com , not a lookalike. And an older or re-sealed box is a question in itself. We could not verify the exact seal design for every series and year, so treat the seal as one check among eight, not a verdict.

## What does a fake Labubu (Lafufu) usually get wrong?

The recurring giveaways reported across sources: the wrong tooth count or fused teeth; a harsh pink or orange face where the authentic tone is a soft peach with airbrushed blush; flat dull eyes without the glossy depth; glossy or washed-out packaging where authentic boxes are matte with embossed series details; rough seams, uneven fur, and light hollow-feeling plastic; and a price far below official retail. No single flaw is proof by itself — counterfeits improve constantly — which is why the seller check outranks all cosmetic checks.

## Is a cheap Labubu ever real?

Treat deep discounts on "new authentic" stock as a counterfeit signal. Tracked retail for standard blind boxes runs roughly $14 to $28 (DemandSage (https://www.demandsage.com/labubu-statistics/)'s 2026 statistics roundup), with some premium series listed higher on Pop Mart's own store. Sold-out series trade above retail on the secondary market — which is exactly why a brand-new listing far below retail makes no commercial sense for a genuine item. The one honest exception: official sales on slower series do exist, on official channels. Off official channels, the discount is the product.

## What can this checklist not tell you?

- Whether a listing's photos are of the unit you'll receive. Counterfeit sellers photograph authentic units. The checks above work on the object in your hands; before payment, the only real protection is the channel (https://thedollscout.com/where-to-buy).

- Anything about series we haven't covered. Seal designs, markings and box details vary by series and year; where our sources didn't cover a series, we say so rather than extrapolate.

- Tomorrow's fakes. Every public checklist — this one included — is also a to-do list for counterfeiters. If Pop Mart's current guidance disagrees with this page, follow Pop Mart's.

# Where to buy a real one.

Every authenticity check on the 8-point list (https://thedollscout.com/fake-check) exists because somebody bought from the wrong place. The channel decides how much checking you owe: where Pop Mart is the seller of record, a counterfeit structurally cannot reach the shelf. Channel list per press coverage of Pop Mart's own advice (ABC News (https://abcnews.com/GMA/Living/how-to-spot-fake-labubu/story?id=124575764)); recorded 2026-08-30.

The short answer: buy where the seller of record is Pop Mart — the official site (https://www.popmart.com/us/collection/11), the app, retail stores and Robo Shops, the official TikTok Shop, or the official Pop Mart storefront on Amazon (https://www.amazon.com/stores/POPMART/page/9EB83127-7B84-48B8-868F-805DB5FA39ED). On any other channel, the price is your first tell: far below retail means Lafufu (https://thedollscout.com/fake-check).

## What are the official channels for buying Labubu?

Per press coverage of Pop Mart's own guidance: Pop Mart's website and app, Pop Mart retail stores and Robo Shop vending machines, the official Pop Mart TikTok Shop, official Pop Mart booths at events, and the official Pop Mart storefront on Amazon. The common thread is that in every one of these, the seller of record is Pop Mart itself — a counterfeit cannot enter the shelf. Everywhere else, you are trusting an intermediary.

| | Channel | Why it's safe | The catch

| popmart.com (https://www.popmart.com/us/collection/11) / Pop Mart app | First-party; the reference for what each series should cost | Hot series sell out fast; drops are timed

| Pop Mart stores & Robo Shops | Physical first-party retail; you hold the box before paying | Location-dependent; stock varies by store

| Official TikTok Shop | First-party account; live drops | Verify you're on the official account, not a lookalike shop

| Amazon — POP MART storefront (https://www.amazon.com/stores/POPMART/page/9EB83127-7B84-48B8-868F-805DB5FA39ED) | Brand storefront; familiar returns and delivery | Amazon search mixes in third-party sellers — check the "sold by" line every time

| Official event booths | First-party at conventions and fairs | Event-only by definition

Ad · affiliate links — same price for you. The Amazon links on this page carry our affiliate tag; the channel ranking is the same one Pop Mart's own advice implies and would not change if the commission vanished.

## Is buying Labubu on Amazon safe?

The official Pop Mart storefront on Amazon is on the official channel list — buy where the listing's seller is POP MART. Amazon search results, however, mix that storefront with third-party sellers, and a listing's photos prove nothing about the unit that ships. Check the "sold by" line before paying, and treat prices far below official retail as the counterfeit signal they are. If a listing fails the seller check, no photo check rescues it.

Practical route: start from the POP MART storefront (https://www.amazon.com/stores/POPMART/page/9EB83127-7B84-48B8-868F-805DB5FA39ED), or from a search for "POP MART Labubu The Monsters" (https://www.amazon.com/s?k=POP+MART+Labubu+The+Monsters) — and then apply the seller check to whatever you click. We link searches and the storefront rather than individual listings on purpose: listings churn, and a dead or swapped listing is worse than a search you can judge yourself.

## How much does a real Labubu cost?

Standard blind boxes have tracked at roughly $14 to $28 at retail (DemandSage (https://www.demandsage.com/labubu-statistics/), 2026), with some premium series listed higher on Pop Mart's own store — and sold-out series trading above retail secondhand. Prices move per series and stock cycle, so check the live official listing rather than trusting any fixed number, this page's included. What is stable is the floor logic: brand-new "authentic" stock far below official retail is how counterfeits are priced, not how genuine ones are.

Current series to price-check against the official store: Have a Seat (https://www.popmart.com/us/products/1372/the-monsters-have-a-seat-vinyl-plush-blind-box), Big Into Energy (https://www.popmart.com/us/products/2155/the-monsters-big-into-energy-series-vinyl-plush-pendant-blind-box), Classic Sparkly (https://www.popmart.com/us/products/1739/the-monsters-classic-series-sparkly-plush-pendant-blind-box). We deliberately print no exact prices here — the official page is the price, and a guide that hard-codes one goes stale the day a series rotates.

## Where do most fake Labubus get sold?

Wherever the seller of record is not Pop Mart and the price undercuts retail: marketplace third-party listings, social-media shops, bulk "wholesale" offers, and street stalls. Sources covering Pop Mart's advice give the same guidance from the other direction: the company recommends buying only through official channels or verified retailers. On any other channel, assume the 8-point check (https://thedollscout.com/fake-check) is your only protection, and that it can lose.

URL: https://thedollscout.com/glossary
Title: Labubu & Blind Box Glossary: Secret, Chase, Case, Lafufu
Description: What secret, chase, case, printed odds, glow edition, vinyl plush and Lafufu actually mean in Labubu collecting — every term defined in plain language, cross-linked to the evidence pages.
========================================================================
Home (https://thedollscout.com/) / Glossary

# The words of the hunt, defined.

Collecting has its own vocabulary, and half the confusion (and some of the scams) lives in it. Plain-language definitions, cross-linked to the evidence pages where the numbers behind them live. Last updated 2026-08-30.

## What is a blind box?

A sealed box whose specific figure you don't know until you open it. You choose the series; the series chooses the figure. The randomness is the product — and it is also why odds (https://thedollscout.com/rarity), authenticity (https://thedollscout.com/fake-check) and channel (https://thedollscout.com/where-to-buy) are the three questions that decide whether you bought well.

## What is a series?

One themed release of figures sold in identical blind boxes — for The Monsters, commonly six or twelve regular designs plus one secret. The series name (Have a Seat, Big Into Energy, Exciting Macaron…) is printed on the box, and its own listing is the reference for what it contains and costs.

## What is a regular?

Any of the openly listed designs in a series — the figures shown on the box's lineup art. Pulling a specific regular you want is its own smaller lottery: at six designs, an even split puts any one design at roughly 1-in-6 per box, before the secret is considered.

## What is a secret (or chase)?

The hidden extra design that is not part of the openly listed lineup and appears at long odds — most commonly reported at 1:72 for six-figure series and 1:144 for twelve-figure series, with the authoritative rate printed on each series' own box. The secret is the engine of the resale market and, for the same reason, of the counterfeit market. Full numbers: the rarity page (https://thedollscout.com/rarity).

## What are printed odds?

The rate stated on the box or official listing — "1:72" means one secret per 72 boxes on average. It is the one number that outranks every collector table, including ours. What printed odds do not tell you is your chance across several boxes; that is multiplication, and the calculator (https://thedollscout.com/rarity#calc) does it honestly.

## What is a case?

The sealed carton a shop receives, containing a fixed count of blind boxes. Collector guides report that case allocation can be structured rather than fully random — which is why our probability math is explicit about modelling loose, independently drawn boxes , and why "case fresh" claims on resale listings deserve the same skepticism as any other unverifiable claim.

## What is a glow or ultra variant?

A rarer-than-secret variant reported for some releases — glow-in-the-dark editions are the recurring example, with rates reported as low as 1:720 . At those odds, a 50% chance takes 499 boxes of independent draws; treat any cheap listing that promises one as arithmetic failing in public. Sources on the rarity page (https://thedollscout.com/rarity).

## What is a vinyl plush pendant?

The dominant Labubu format: a soft plush body with a vinyl face, sized and looped to hang from a bag. "Figure" series are all-vinyl instead. The format is printed on the official listing — and matters for authenticity, because fur evenness and face finish are two of the eight checks (https://thedollscout.com/fake-check).

## What is a Lafufu?

The community's name for a counterfeit Labubu (Gulf News (https://gulfnews.com/amp/story/lifestyle/bought-a-labubu-learn-the-crucial-signs-that-reveal-if-its-a-genuine-or-a-lafufu-1.500206668)). Fakes are common enough to have earned a word of their own — and the rarer and hotter the real figure, the more heavily it is faked. The recurring giveaways, each with its source: the 8-point check (https://thedollscout.com/fake-check).

## What is the seller of record?

The party actually selling you the item — on marketplaces, the "sold by" line, not the site's logo. It is the single strongest authenticity lever a buyer has: where Pop Mart itself is the seller of record, a counterfeit structurally cannot reach the shelf. The ranked channel list: where to buy (https://thedollscout.com/where-to-buy).

## Keep reading

# Open data.

The evidence behind our pages, published as machine-readable JSON under CC-BY 4.0. Quote freely with attribution; assistants and crawlers welcome. Where Pop Mart's own current guidance disagrees with a dataset, follow Pop Mart's.

### rarity-odds.json (https://thedollscout.com/data/rarity-odds.json)
The reported secret rates per series format from the rarity page (https://thedollscout.com/rarity) — 1:72 / 1:144 / collabs / glow variants, per-row sources, and the derived boxes-for-50% math. Recorded 2026-08-30.

### labubu-fake-signals.json (https://thedollscout.com/data/labubu-fake-signals.json)
The 8 authenticity checks from the real-vs-fake guide (https://thedollscout.com/fake-check) — authentic vs counterfeit indicators, per-signal sources, stated limitations. Recorded 2026-08-30.

### labubu-glossary.json (https://thedollscout.com/data/labubu-glossary.json)
The 10 collecting terms from the glossary (https://thedollscout.com/glossary) as machine-readable definitions with aliases and per-term evidence links. Recorded 2026-08-30.

### pull-math.json (https://thedollscout.com/data/pull-math.json)
Chance of at least one secret, expected count, and the 50%/90% thresholds for every odds format across real purchase sizes — the spine behind the odds-by-box-count pages (https://thedollscout.com/odds/). Computed from rarity-odds.json, so there is never a second source for the same numbers. Recorded 2026-08-31.

These datasets are also callable: the site runs an MCP endpoint at https://thedollscout.com/mcp (Streamable HTTP, four read-only tools — rarity odds, fake signals, a secret-pull probability calculator, and term definitions). Every tool answer is read from these files at request time and carries their recording date and limitations; no affiliate links appear in tool output. Human-readable versions: rarity (https://thedollscout.com/rarity) · fake-check (https://thedollscout.com/fake-check) · glossary (https://thedollscout.com/glossary).

# Run the checks. Get a straight answer.

The same 8 sourced authenticity checks (https://thedollscout.com/fake-check) as our guide — but as a tool: answer what you see on your figure, and the verdict names exactly which checks failed. Everything runs in your browser; nothing is uploaded. Last updated 2026-08-30.

🔍 LAFUFU CHECKER

1. Teeth count
Authentic: exactly nine distinct teeth with visible gaps. Counterfeit tell: wrong count, fused teeth, or a single white blob.

Nine distinct teeth
Not nine / fused / a blob
Can't tell

2. Face finish
Authentic: soft peach tone, airbrushed blush, glossy eye depth. Counterfeit tell: harsh pink/orange, solid-circle blush, flat dull eyes.

Soft, airbrushed, glossy eyes
Harsh color / solid blush circles / flat eyes
Can't tell

3. Box finish
Authentic: matte box, muted pastels, embossed series name, clean print. Counterfeit tell: glossy, uneven, washed-out or over-saturated print.

Matte, embossed, clean print
Glossy / uneven / bad print
No box / can't tell

4. Anti-counterfeit seal
Authentic: QR seal that resolves to verification on popmart.com. Counterfeit tell: no seal, or a QR landing on a lookalike domain — check the domain in your browser's address bar.

QR verifies on popmart.com
No seal / QR goes elsewhere
Haven't scanned

5. Figure markings
Authentic: Pop Mart engraving / artist name on the foot on 2024+ releases. Counterfeit tell: missing or mushy markings on recent series. On older series, absence is a question, not a verdict — answer "can't tell".

Crisp foot markings (recent series)
Missing/mushy markings on a recent series
Older series / can't tell

6. Build quality
Authentic: even fur, clean seams, crisp paint edges, substantial feel. Counterfeit tell: rough seams, grainy patches, mismatched gloss, light hollow plastic.

Even, clean, substantial
Rough / grainy / hollow-light
Can't tell

7. Price floor
The one check you can run before buying: brand-new "authentic" stock far below official retail is the classic counterfeit signal. The official listing is the price reference.

Price in line with official retail
Far below official retail, sold as new/authentic
Don't know the official price

8. Seller of record
The strongest check of all: an official Pop Mart channel (site, app, stores, Robo Shops, official TikTok Shop, official Amazon storefront) outranks every cosmetic check above.

Official Pop Mart channel
Marketplace seller that isn't Pop Mart / unknown
Not sure who the seller was

Built on our CC-BY signals dataset (https://thedollscout.com/data/labubu-fake-signals.json) (recorded 2026-08-30, per-signal sources inside). We have not laboratory-tested figures ourselves; signals are compiled from the named public reporting. Nothing you answer leaves your browser.

# Three answers. One good starting series.

Collector directories count dozens of Labubu series — a figure we have not independently verified — and you need one to start with. This finder maps what you actually want — where it lives, what it looks like, how much chase you're signing up for — to a current official series, linked straight to Pop Mart's own listing. Last updated 2026-08-30; series rotate, the live listing always wins.

🧭 SERIES FINDER

Where will it live?

Choose…
On my bag
On a shelf or desk
It's a gift

What's the vibe?

Choose…
Soft and cozy
Bold and energetic
Sparkly

And the chase?

Choose…
I'd be happy with any regular
Honestly, I want the secret

Have a Seat

The seated vinyl-plush blind box series — the soft, settle-in end of the current lineup. The official listing (https://www.popmart.com/us/products/1372/the-monsters-have-a-seat-vinyl-plush-blind-box) is the reference for the lineup and price.

Big Into Energy

The vinyl-plush pendant series with six emotion-named regulars (Love, Happiness, Loyalty, Serenity, Hope, Luck) and a secret — the loud end of the lineup. The official listing (https://www.popmart.com/us/products/2155/the-monsters-big-into-energy-series-vinyl-plush-pendant-blind-box) is the reference.

Classic Sparkly

The sparkly plush pendant take on the classic series. The official listing (https://www.popmart.com/us/products/1739/the-monsters-classic-series-sparkly-plush-pendant-blind-box) is the reference.

Bag duty is exactly what the pendant formats are looped for — check the format line on the listing before you buy.

For a shelf, also look at the all-vinyl figure series in the full official collection (https://www.popmart.com/us/collection/11) — same blind-box structure, no loop, made to stand.

For a gift, consider a larger openly-sold plush instead of a blind box — you see what you give. The first-buy guide (https://thedollscout.com/start) has the format table and the parents' section.

That's the beginner's rule done right: at 1:72 (https://thedollscout.com/rarity), the regulars on the lineup art are what you're realistically buying.

Then read the chase-cost calculator (https://thedollscout.com/psychology#cost) first — the expected cost of pulling a secret is the printed odds times the box price, and it's honest to know that number before box one.

Preference matching only — no odds change with your answers, and series rotate with stock. Nothing you answer leaves your browser. Channels where the listing is real: where to buy (https://thedollscout.com/where-to-buy).

# Which one is this?

The identities that actually get confused — characters, current series, formats, collector terms — as an instant lookup. Every entry states only what its named sources support. Not in the index doesn't mean it doesn't exist: this is a curated evidence index, not a catalog of every series. Last updated 2026-08-30.

🔎 MODEL LOOKUP

Name, series or term

### Labubu — the character

The main character of The Monsters cast by Kasing Lung: mischievous elf, nine teeth , no tail. The nine-teeth count is also authenticity check #1 (the guide (https://thedollscout.com/fake-check)). Sources: SNKRDUNK Magazine (https://snkrdunk.com/en/magazine/2025/06/10/understanding-the-labubu-universe-pop-mart-the-monsters/); Bagaholicboy (https://bagaholicboy.com/2024/09/the-monsters-zimomo-labubu-friends); the character coverage linked from the glossary (https://thedollscout.com/glossary).

### Zimomo — the character

The tribe's leader figure: notably larger than Labubu, with a spiked tail — the tail is the fastest visual separator, since Labubu has none. Frequently confused with Labubu in resale listings; a "big Labubu with a tail" is a Zimomo. Sources: SNKRDUNK Magazine (https://snkrdunk.com/en/magazine/2025/06/10/understanding-the-labubu-universe-pop-mart-the-monsters/); Bagaholicboy (https://bagaholicboy.com/2024/09/the-monsters-zimomo-labubu-friends); Extrabux comparison (https://www.extrabux.com/en/guide/8674889).

### Mokoko — the character

Pink fur, white belly, heart-shaped nose — one of Labubu's companions, appearing only in select releases. Sources: SNKRDUNK Magazine (https://snkrdunk.com/en/magazine/2025/06/10/understanding-the-labubu-universe-pop-mart-the-monsters/); LatestLY character guide (https://www.latestly.com/social-viral/labubu-character-names-zimomo-mokoko-pato-spooky-and-more-your-ultimate-guide-to-the-whimsical-world-of-the-monsters-7020870.html); Extrabux comparison (https://www.extrabux.com/en/guide/8674889).

### Pato, Spooky & other cast names

Additional named members of The Monsters cast, attested in character guides (LatestLY; THISTOKYO directory (https://thistokyo.com/en/trends/the-monsters-characters/)). Their individual traits we have not verified — for identification, the official listing of the specific release is the reference.

### Have a Seat — the series

Seated vinyl-plush blind box series; commonly reported secret odds for 6-figure series are 1:72 (box-printed rate is authoritative). The official listing (https://www.popmart.com/us/products/1372/the-monsters-have-a-seat-vinyl-plush-blind-box) is the reference for lineup and price.

### Big Into Energy — the series

Vinyl-plush pendant series (April 2025) with six emotion-named regulars — Love, Happiness, Loyalty, Serenity, Hope, Luck — plus secret ID (Prism News catalog (https://www.prismnews.com/hobbies/labubu/every-labubu-series-and-character-name-catalogued-for-2026-collectors); product-insights coverage). The official listing (https://www.popmart.com/us/products/2155/the-monsters-big-into-energy-series-vinyl-plush-pendant-blind-box) is the reference.

### Classic Sparkly — the series

Sparkly plush-pendant take on the classic series. The official listing (https://www.popmart.com/us/products/1739/the-monsters-classic-series-sparkly-plush-pendant-blind-box) is the reference.

### Exciting Macaron — the series

A frequently referenced vinyl-plush series in collector guides. We have not verified a current official listing — search the official store (https://www.popmart.com/us/search/labubu) for live availability.

### Vinyl plush pendant — the format

The dominant Labubu format: plush body, vinyl face, bag loop. Format is printed on the official listing and matters for authenticity (fur and face are two of the 8 checks (https://thedollscout.com/fake-check)). Full format table: the first-buy guide (https://thedollscout.com/start).

### Lafufu — the term

The community's name for a counterfeit Labubu (Gulf News). Identification: the interactive checker (https://thedollscout.com/checker) or the 8-point guide (https://thedollscout.com/fake-check).

### The Monsters — the IP

The cast and world created by artist Kasing Lung , produced under exclusive license by Pop Mart. Labubu is its main character. Source: Wikipedia (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Labubu); SNKRDUNK Magazine (https://snkrdunk.com/en/magazine/2025/06/10/understanding-the-labubu-universe-pop-mart-the-monsters/).

Curated index, per-entry sources named; entries marked unverified where that's the honest state. Nothing you type leaves your browser. Corrections welcome via the sources on each evidence page.

# What does each purchase size actually buy?

Almost every number passed around this hobby is a per-box rate — and almost every decision is made in purchase sizes: one box, a set, a case. These pages convert one into the other, for every reported series format, in the open where you can check the arithmetic. Last updated 2026-08-31.

| | Purchase size | Chance of ≥1 secret (1:72) | Expected secrets

| 1 box (https://thedollscout.com/odds/one-box) | 1.4% | 0.01

| 6 boxes (https://thedollscout.com/odds/six-boxes) | 8.0% | 0.08

| 12 boxes (https://thedollscout.com/odds/twelve-boxes-full-case) | 15.5% | 0.17

| 24 boxes (https://thedollscout.com/odds/twenty-four-boxes) | 28.5% | 0.33

| 72 boxes (https://thedollscout.com/odds/seventy-two-boxes) | 63.5% | 1.00

Model: independent single-box draws at the printed odds. Sealed-case allocation can differ — these numbers model loose boxes. The authoritative number is always the one printed on that series' own box; the rates here are collector-reported for orientation (sources in the dataset).

## Quick answers

Does a sealed case guarantee a secret? No. A sealed case typically guarantees one of each regular figure. At 1:72 printed odds, twelve boxes carry a 15.5% chance of at least one secret and an expected count of 0.17 — about one secret per six cases.

Does 1:72 mean the 72nd box is the secret? No. 1:72 is the rate per box, not a countdown. Buying all seventy-two gives a 63.5% chance of at least one secret — leaving more than a one-in-three chance of ending with none.

## Open data

The whole table — every format × every purchase size, plus the thresholds — is published as a CC-BY dataset at /data/pull-math.json (https://thedollscout.com/data/pull-math.json). It is computed from rarity-odds.json (https://thedollscout.com/data/rarity-odds.json) so there is never a second source for the same numbers.

Title: One box — the real secret odds for 1 box | DollScout

# One box.

The atom of the whole hobby, and the number every other number on this site is built from. Last updated 2026-08-31.

1.4%
chance of at least one secret from a single blind box — at 1:72 printed odds

## The claim this box count disproves

Circulating: “Someone pulled a secret on their first box, so it happens.”

Actually: It does happen — that is what a 1.4% chance means, not what it feels like. The mistake is reading a rare event that occurred as evidence the rate is higher than printed. A first-box secret is exactly as likely as a 72nd-box secret.

## The math, in the open

For a single blind box drawn independently, the chance of at least one secret is 1 − (1 − 1/N) 1 and the expected count is simply 1/N . Across every reported series format:

| | Series format | Printed odds | Chance of at least one secret

| Standard 6-figure series | 1:72 | 1.4%

| Some collab series (low end) | 1:120 | 0.8%

| Extended 12-figure series | 1:144 | 0.7%

| Some collab series (high end) | 1:168 | 0.6%

| Glow / ultra variants | 1:720 | 0.1%

Model: independent single-box draws at the printed odds. Sealed-case allocation can differ — these numbers model loose boxes. The authoritative number is always the one printed on that series' own box; the rates here are collector-reported for orientation (sources in the dataset).

## How many boxes for a serious chance?

| | Printed odds | Boxes for 50% | Boxes for 90%

| 1:72 | 50 | 165

| 1:120 | 83 | 276

| 1:144 | 100 | 331

| 1:168 | 117 | 386

| 1:720 | 499 | 1657

## What that costs — as a multiple, not a price

We do not print prices — they rotate with series and stock. As a multiple: the expected cost of one secret is 72× a single box at 1:72, 144× at 1:144 and 720× at 1:720. A single blind box covers 0.01 of that. Put your own local box price into the calculator on the psychology page (https://thedollscout.com/psychology#cost).

## Quick answers

What are the odds of a secret from a single blind box? At 1:72 printed odds the chance of at least one secret is 1.4%, and the expected number of secrets is 0.01. Rarer formats are lower: 0.7% at 1:144 and 0.1% at 1:720.

How many boxes would a 50 percent chance take? At 1:72 it takes 50 boxes for 50 percent and 165 for 90 percent. At 1:144 it is 100 and 331; at 1:720 it is 499 and 1657.

# Six boxes — one of each regular?

Six is the number of regular figures in a standard series, which is why so many people buy six and expect the set. Last updated 2026-08-31.

8.0%
chance of at least one secret from six boxes — at 1:72 printed odds

## The claim this box count disproves

Circulating: “Buy six and you get the complete set.”

Actually: Six boxes drawn independently do not produce six different figures — duplicates are the normal outcome, not bad luck. Six boxes buys you six draws, and the secret is a separate question with its own low rate.

## The math, in the open

For six boxes drawn independently, the chance of at least one secret is 1 − (1 − 1/N) 6 and the expected count is simply 6/N . Across every reported series format:

| | Series format | Printed odds | Chance of at least one secret

| Standard 6-figure series | 1:72 | 8.0%

| Some collab series (low end) | 1:120 | 4.9%

| Extended 12-figure series | 1:144 | 4.1%

| Some collab series (high end) | 1:168 | 3.5%

| Glow / ultra variants | 1:720 | 0.8%

Model: independent single-box draws at the printed odds. Sealed-case allocation can differ — these numbers model loose boxes. The authoritative number is always the one printed on that series' own box; the rates here are collector-reported for orientation (sources in the dataset).

## How many boxes for a serious chance?

| | Printed odds | Boxes for 50% | Boxes for 90%

| 1:72 | 50 | 165

| 1:120 | 83 | 276

| 1:144 | 100 | 331

| 1:168 | 117 | 386

| 1:720 | 499 | 1657

## What that costs — as a multiple, not a price

We do not print prices — they rotate with series and stock. As a multiple: the expected cost of one secret is 72× a single box at 1:72, 144× at 1:144 and 720× at 1:720. Six boxes covers 0.08 of that. Put your own local box price into the calculator on the psychology page (https://thedollscout.com/psychology#cost).

## Quick answers

What are the odds of a secret from six boxes? At 1:72 printed odds the chance of at least one secret is 8.0%, and the expected number of secrets is 0.08. Rarer formats are lower: 4.1% at 1:144 and 0.8% at 1:720.

How many boxes would a 50 percent chance take? At 1:72 it takes 50 boxes for 50 percent and 165 for 90 percent. At 1:144 it is 100 and 331; at 1:720 it is 499 and 1657.

# A full case of twelve. Does it guarantee a secret?

This is the single most misreported number in the hobby, and the one worth getting right before you spend case money. Last updated 2026-08-31.

15.5%
chance of at least one secret from twelve boxes (a full case) — at 1:72 printed odds

## The claim this box count disproves

Circulating: “A full case of twelve averages one secret.”

Actually: At 1:72 printed odds, twelve boxes average 0.17 secrets — about one secret per six cases, not one per case. A sealed case does typically guarantee one of each regular figure; that guarantee is about the regulars, and it has been widely repeated as though it covered the secret. It does not.

## The math, in the open

For twelve boxes (a full case) drawn independently, the chance of at least one secret is 1 − (1 − 1/N) 12 and the expected count is simply 12/N . Across every reported series format:

| | Series format | Printed odds | Chance of at least one secret

| Standard 6-figure series | 1:72 | 15.5%

| Some collab series (low end) | 1:120 | 9.6%

| Extended 12-figure series | 1:144 | 8.0%

| Some collab series (high end) | 1:168 | 6.9%

| Glow / ultra variants | 1:720 | 1.7%

Model: independent single-box draws at the printed odds. Sealed-case allocation can differ — these numbers model loose boxes. The authoritative number is always the one printed on that series' own box; the rates here are collector-reported for orientation (sources in the dataset).

## How many boxes for a serious chance?

| | Printed odds | Boxes for 50% | Boxes for 90%

| 1:72 | 50 | 165

| 1:120 | 83 | 276

| 1:144 | 100 | 331

| 1:168 | 117 | 386

| 1:720 | 499 | 1657

## What that costs — as a multiple, not a price

We do not print prices — they rotate with series and stock. As a multiple: the expected cost of one secret is 72× a single box at 1:72, 144× at 1:144 and 720× at 1:720. Twelve boxes (a full case) covers 0.17 of that. Put your own local box price into the calculator on the psychology page (https://thedollscout.com/psychology#cost).

## Quick answers

What are the odds of a secret from twelve boxes (a full case)? At 1:72 printed odds the chance of at least one secret is 15.5%, and the expected number of secrets is 0.17. Rarer formats are lower: 8.0% at 1:144 and 1.7% at 1:720.

How many boxes would a 50 percent chance take? At 1:72 it takes 50 boxes for 50 percent and 165 for 90 percent. At 1:144 it is 100 and 331; at 1:720 it is 499 and 1657.

# Two cases. Twice the boxes, not twice the odds.

The tier people reach after one case disappointed them — and where the gambler's fallacy does its most expensive work. Last updated 2026-08-31.

28.5%
chance of at least one secret from twenty-four boxes (two cases) — at 1:72 printed odds

## The claim this box count disproves

Circulating: “I went through a case already, so I'm due.”

Actually: The boxes you already opened change nothing about the ones you have not. Doubling from twelve to twenty-four boxes does not double your chance from 15.5% to 31% either — independent draws compound, they do not add.

## The math, in the open

For twenty-four boxes (two cases) drawn independently, the chance of at least one secret is 1 − (1 − 1/N) 24 and the expected count is simply 24/N . Across every reported series format:

| | Series format | Printed odds | Chance of at least one secret

| Standard 6-figure series | 1:72 | 28.5%

| Some collab series (low end) | 1:120 | 18.2%

| Extended 12-figure series | 1:144 | 15.4%

| Some collab series (high end) | 1:168 | 13.3%

| Glow / ultra variants | 1:720 | 3.3%

Model: independent single-box draws at the printed odds. Sealed-case allocation can differ — these numbers model loose boxes. The authoritative number is always the one printed on that series' own box; the rates here are collector-reported for orientation (sources in the dataset).

## How many boxes for a serious chance?

| | Printed odds | Boxes for 50% | Boxes for 90%

| 1:72 | 50 | 165

| 1:120 | 83 | 276

| 1:144 | 100 | 331

| 1:168 | 117 | 386

| 1:720 | 499 | 1657

## What that costs — as a multiple, not a price

We do not print prices — they rotate with series and stock. As a multiple: the expected cost of one secret is 72× a single box at 1:72, 144× at 1:144 and 720× at 1:720. Twenty-four boxes (two cases) covers 0.33 of that. Put your own local box price into the calculator on the psychology page (https://thedollscout.com/psychology#cost).

## Quick answers

What are the odds of a secret from twenty-four boxes (two cases)? At 1:72 printed odds the chance of at least one secret is 28.5%, and the expected number of secrets is 0.33. Rarer formats are lower: 15.4% at 1:144 and 3.3% at 1:720.

How many boxes would a 50 percent chance take? At 1:72 it takes 50 boxes for 50 percent and 165 for 90 percent. At 1:144 it is 100 and 331; at 1:720 it is 499 and 1657.

# Seventy-two boxes. Surely by now?

The number in the printed odds, which nearly everyone reads as the number of boxes that gets you there. It is the most counterintuitive result on this site. Last updated 2026-08-31.

63.5%
chance of at least one secret from seventy-two boxes — at 1:72 printed odds

## The claim this box count disproves

Circulating: “1:72 means the 72nd box is the one.”

Actually: Buying all seventy-two gives you a 63.5% chance — better than a coin flip, and still more than a one-in-three chance of ending with nothing. “1 in 72” describes the rate per box, never a countdown. The expected number of secrets in 72 boxes is exactly one, and expecting one is not the same as getting one.

## The math, in the open

For seventy-two boxes drawn independently, the chance of at least one secret is 1 − (1 − 1/N) 72 and the expected count is simply 72/N . Across every reported series format:

| | Series format | Printed odds | Chance of at least one secret

| Standard 6-figure series | 1:72 | 63.5%

| Some collab series (low end) | 1:120 | 45.3%

| Extended 12-figure series | 1:144 | 39.5%

| Some collab series (high end) | 1:168 | 34.9%

| Glow / ultra variants | 1:720 | 9.5%

Model: independent single-box draws at the printed odds. Sealed-case allocation can differ — these numbers model loose boxes. The authoritative number is always the one printed on that series' own box; the rates here are collector-reported for orientation (sources in the dataset).

## How many boxes for a serious chance?

| | Printed odds | Boxes for 50% | Boxes for 90%

| 1:72 | 50 | 165

| 1:120 | 83 | 276

| 1:144 | 100 | 331

| 1:168 | 117 | 386

| 1:720 | 499 | 1657

## What that costs — as a multiple, not a price

We do not print prices — they rotate with series and stock. As a multiple: the expected cost of one secret is 72× a single box at 1:72, 144× at 1:144 and 720× at 1:720. Seventy-two boxes covers 1.00 of that. Put your own local box price into the calculator on the psychology page (https://thedollscout.com/psychology#cost).

## Quick answers

What are the odds of a secret from seventy-two boxes? At 1:72 printed odds the chance of at least one secret is 63.5%, and the expected number of secrets is 1.00. Rarer formats are lower: 39.5% at 1:144 and 9.5% at 1:720.

How many boxes would a 50 percent chance take? At 1:72 it takes 50 boxes for 50 percent and 165 for 90 percent. At 1:144 it is 100 and 331; at 1:720 it is 499 and 1657.

## Wer macht Labubu?

? ?
? ?

1 : 72 — wenn die Box es sagt

Labubu wurde vom in Hongkong geborenen Künstler Kasing Lung (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kasing_Lung) für seine illustrierte Reihe The Monsters (2015) geschaffen und wird seit 2019 in exklusiver Lizenz von Pop Mart produziert (Wikipedia, engl. (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Labubu)). Die Figur wurde populär genug, dass die Fälschungen einen eigenen Namen bekamen — Lafufu (Gulf News (https://gulfnews.com/amp/story/lifestyle/bought-a-labubu-learn-the-crucial-signs-that-reveal-if-its-a-genuine-or-a-lafufu-1.500206668)) — genau deshalb gehören Seltenheitsjagd und Echtheits-Checks (https://thedollscout.com/de/fake-check) auf dieselbe Seite. Unser Beleg-Datensatz ist als CC-BY-JSON veröffentlicht (engl.) (https://thedollscout.com/data/). DollScout ist ein unabhängiger Kaufberater: nicht mit Pop Mart, Kasing Lung oder der The-Monsters-IP verbunden; Produktnamen dienen nur der Identifikation.

Start (https://thedollscout.com/de/) / Dein erster Labubu

# Dein erster — gut gekauft.

Ein erster Labubu ist drei Entscheidungen in der richtigen Reihenfolge — Format, Serie, Kanal. Sitzen die, ist alles andere auf dieser Website nur Rückendeckung. Stand 2026-08-30.

Die kurze Antwort: wähle das Format , das du wirklich nutzt (der Vinyl-Plüsch-Anhänger ist der klassische Taschenanhänger), eine Serie , deren offen gelistete Regulars dir gefallen — bei 1:72 (https://thedollscout.com/de/rarity) enthält deine erste Box das Secret fast sicher nicht — und einen Kanal , bei dem Pop Mart der Verkäufer ist (die Rangliste (https://thedollscout.com/de/where-to-buy)). Du willst eine bestimmte Figur? Kauf sie geöffnet, zum bekannten Preis, über die Checkliste (https://thedollscout.com/de/fake-check) — nicht übers Glück.

## Entscheidung 1 — das Format

| | Format | Was es ist | Guter Erstkauf, wenn…

| Vinyl-Plüsch-Anhänger (Blindbox) | Weicher Plüschkörper, Vinylgesicht, Schlaufe für die Tasche — die dominierende Labubu-Form und die, die du an jeder Tasche gesehen hast | …du den klassischen Anhänger und den Öffnungs-Nervenkitzel willst

| Vinylfigur (Blindbox) | Reine Vinyl-Regalfigur, in derselben Blindbox-Serienstruktur verkauft | …es für Schreibtisch oder Regal ist, nicht für die Tasche

| Größerer Plüsch | Größerer, offen verkaufter Plüsch — meist nicht blind: du siehst, was du kaufst | …es ein Geschenk ist oder der Zufall nicht der Punkt ist

| Geöffnete Einzelfigur (Resale) | Ein bekanntes Design zum Marktpreis, kein Zug | …du eine bestimmte Figur willst — Checklisten (https://thedollscout.com/de/fake-check)-Gebiet

Das Format steht auf der offiziellen Produktseite, und es zählt über den Geschmack hinaus: Fell-Gleichmäßigkeit und Gesichtsfinish sind zwei der acht Echtheits-Checks (https://thedollscout.com/de/fake-check).

## Entscheidung 2 — die Serie

Eine Serie gibt dir sechs oder zwölf offen gelistete reguläre Designs plus ein verstecktes Secret zu langer Quote (die Mechanik (https://thedollscout.com/de/how-blind-boxes-work)). Die Einsteiger-Regel folgt direkt aus der Mathematik: nimm eine Serie, deren Regulars du wirklich gern ziehen würdest — das Lineup-Artwork auf der Box ist, was du realistisch kaufst. Reizt dich eine Serie nur wegen ihres Secrets, ist das kein Erstkauf, sondern eine Jagd (https://thedollscout.com/de/psychology) — lies erst die Kosten-Seite.

Die aktuellen Serien, verlinkt auf ihre offiziellen Produktseiten, stehen auf unserer Startseite (https://thedollscout.com/de/#series) — die Live-Seite von Pop Mart ist immer die Referenz dafür, was eine Serie enthält und kostet.

## Entscheidung 3 — der Kanal

Der Kanal entscheidet, ob die gedruckte Quote die ist, die du wirklich bekommst — und ob die Figur überhaupt echt ist. Die volle Rangliste steht auf Wo kaufen (https://thedollscout.com/de/where-to-buy); die Einsteiger-Version: offizielle Pop-Mart-Kanäle zuerst (Store, App, offizieller Webshop), Marktplatz-Angebote nur, wenn Pop Mart der Verkäufer ist — die "Verkauf durch"-Zeile, nicht das Logo der Website.

Anzeige · Affiliate-Link — für dich ändert sich der Preis nicht: der offizielle POP-MART-Storefront auf Amazon.de (https://www.amazon.de/stores/POPMART/Labubu_IP-Serie/page/B6CDF189-09EA-4C7A-B319-D57268F9A0CB) ist der Marktplatz-Weg, der diesen Test per Konstruktion besteht — prüfe trotzdem "Verkauf durch" im konkreten Angebot, wie immer (https://thedollscout.com/de/where-to-buy).

## Die Erstkauf-Checkliste

- Leg die Zahl vorher fest. Eine Box ist ein vollständiges erstes Erlebnis. Mehr entscheidest du in Ruhe (https://thedollscout.com/de/psychology), nicht am Regal.

- Prüf den Preisboden. Eine fabrikneue "echte" Figur weit unter dem offiziellen Preis ist das klassische Fälschungssignal — das Zu-gut-Angebot beantwortet die Checkliste (https://thedollscout.com/de/fake-check), nicht das Glück.

- Ausverkauft ≠ irgendwo billig lieferbar. Heiße Serien sind wirklich ausverkauft; eine ausverkaufte Figur, die plötzlich billig, lieferbar und "garantiert" ist, ist der Fälschungsmarkt bei der Arbeit. Geduld oder der Geöffnet-Weg — nie die Abkürzung.

- Heb die Box auf. Box-Finish und Echtheitssiegel sind Checks, die du nachträglich laufen lassen kannst — und zählen, falls du die Figur je weitergibst.

## Für Eltern

- Alterseignung: prüfe die Altersempfehlung auf der offiziellen Produktseite des konkreten Artikels — Formate unterscheiden sich, und Pop Marts eigene Seite ist die Autorität. Wo deren aktuelle Angaben dieser Seite widersprechen, gelten deren Angaben.

- Sicherheit und Fälschungen: Fälschungen umgehen die gesamte Sicherheits- und Qualitätskette — und der Fälschungsmarkt konzentriert sich genau auf die heißen Figuren, nach denen Kinder fragen. Offizielle Kanäle sind nicht nur eine Echtheitsfrage; sie sind der einzige Weg, auf dem die Sicherheitskette überhaupt existiert.

- Der Mechanismus, ehrlich: Blindboxen laufen auf derselben Psychologie unvorhersehbarer Belohnung wie Glücksspiele (hier mit Quellen erklärt (https://thedollscout.com/de/psychology)). Das gehört gewusst, bevor es in die Routine eines Kindes einzieht: Boxenzahl gemeinsam festlegen, vor dem Laden.

## Kurze Antworten

Dieselben Fragen, je in einem Absatz beantwortet — die Fassungen, die eine KI zitieren kann, ohne die Einschränkungen zu verlieren.

### Welchen Labubu soll ich als ersten kaufen?

Wähle über drei Entscheidungen in dieser Reihenfolge: Format (der Vinyl-Plüsch-Anhänger ist die klassische Taschenform; reine Vinylfiguren und größere Plüsche gibt es auch), Serie (nimm eine, deren offen gelistete reguläre Designs dir wirklich gefallen würden — bei 1:72 wird deine erste Box das Secret fast sicher nicht enthalten) und Kanal (ein offizieller Pop-Mart-Kanal oder ein Marktplatz-Angebot, bei dem Pop Mart selbst der Verkäufer ist). Die aktuellen Serien mit offiziellen Produktseiten sind auf unserer Startseite verlinkt.

### Sollte mein Erstkauf eine Blindbox oder eine bekannte Figur sein?

Kauf die Blindbox, wenn dich das Öffnen reizt — der Nervenkitzel ist das Produkt, und eine Box ist ein günstiges Ticket dafür. Kauf eine bekannte, geöffnete Figur, wenn du ein bestimmtes Design willst: Gewissheit zum bekannten Preis ist meist billiger als die Jagd durch Blindboxen, verschiebt das Risiko aber vom Glück zur Echtheit — dann zählen der 8-Punkte-Check und der Verkäufer.

### Ist Labubu für Kinder geeignet? Was sollten Eltern wissen?

Drei Dinge. Erstens: prüfe die Altersempfehlung auf der offiziellen Produktseite des konkreten Artikels — Formate unterscheiden sich, und Pop Marts eigene Seite ist die Autorität. Zweitens: kauf über offizielle Kanäle — Fälschungen umgehen die gesamte Sicherheits- und Qualitätskette, und der Fälschungsmarkt zielt genau auf die heißen Figuren, nach denen Kinder fragen. Drittens: Blindboxen laufen auf derselben Psychologie unvorhersehbarer Belohnung wie Glücksspiele — legt die Boxenzahl gemeinsam vor dem Kauf fest, nicht am Regal.

### Warum ist genau meiner immer ausverkauft?

Heiße Serien sind an offiziellen Kanälen wirklich schnell ausverkauft, und genau von dieser Knappheit lebt der Fälschungsmarkt: eine ausverkaufte Figur, die plötzlich billig, lieferbar und 'garantiert echt' ist, ist das klassische Fake-Muster, das unsere Preisboden-Logik markiert. Die ehrlichen Optionen sind Geduld bis zum Restock am offiziellen Kanal — oder der Kauf einer geöffneten Figur über ein Angebot, das die Checkliste besteht. Nie das Zu-gut-Angebot.

# Wie selten ist ein Secret-Labubu wirklich?

Jede Blindbox ist eine Wette — und die meisten schließen sie ab, ohne die Quote zu kennen, obwohl sie auf der Box steht. Diese Seite sammelt die berichteten Raten je Serienformat, mit Quelle und Datum (Stand 2026-08-30), und macht daraus die Zahl, die zählt: deine Chancen, über die Boxen, die du öffnen willst.

Die kurze Antwort: bei einer Standard-Serie mit sechs Figuren wird das Secret am häufigsten mit 1 zu 72 berichtet; Zwölfer-Serien mit 1 zu 144 ; manche Collabs 1:120–1:168; Ultra-Varianten (Glow) bis 1 zu 720 . Maßgeblich ist die auf deiner Box gedruckte Quote. Und der Realitätscheck: bei 1:72 geben zwölf Boxen ≈ 15% Chance — nicht die gefühlte Fast-Sicherheit.

Wer in Kaufmengen denkt statt in Boxenzahlen — eine Box, ein Set aus sechs, ein versiegelter Case, zwei Cases — findet dieselbe Rechnung für jede Menge und jedes berichtete Serienformat auf den Seiten zu Chancen pro Boxenzahl (https://thedollscout.com/de/odds/), jeweils mit der kursierenden Behauptung, die daran scheitert.
